findings.specText: Contract NatSpec header (authored story-038, reaffirmed story-043): "Rounding rules: All rounding favors the protocol. Principal is decremented by requested amount, not received amount, so any shortfall accumulates as protocol-owned yield." Inline (line 369-370): "Decrement principal by REQUESTED amount, not RECEIVED amount / Any difference accumulates as protocol-owned yield." story-043 commit a65dbf0: "good execution surfaces as protocol yield."
findings.specSource: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol NatSpec header lines 22-23 + inline comment lines 369-370; git commit a65dbf0 body
findings.actualBehavior: withdraw/_withdrawInternal transfers the FULL ammAdapter swap output `underlyingReceived` to recipient (line 367), then debits principal by the REQUESTED `amount` only (lines 371-372). The documented invariant only holds in the shortfall direction (received < requested). In the over-delivery direction (received > requested), the EXCESS `underlyingReceived - amount` is paid to the recipient/withdrawer, not retained by the strategy.
findings.deviation: The stated invariant 'All rounding favors the protocol' / 'any difference accumulates as protocol-owned yield' is one-directional in code. minOut floors the downside (received >= amount*(1-slip)) but nothing caps the upside. When the Curve-realizable rate is favorable, surplus that the design routes to the protocol via skimSurplus is instead captured by the first client to withdraw — directly contradicting the documented rounding/yield-ownership intent.
findings.crossReference: Same root cause as code-scanner LOCAL-MKT-002 (local-high, uncapped withdraw upside) and profile scannerAttention #2. Exact economic exploitability (is over-delivery realizable on the configured USDe<->sUSDe Curve route, and does a protocol-owned client capturing it constitute a real value leak vs internal transfer) is the econ/interaction scanner's call; reported here as the spec-conformance angle.
findings.recommendation: Cap the underlying transferred to recipient at `amount` (idealUnderlying) and leave the excess in the strategy (held as shares / skimmable surplus), OR amend the design NatSpec to document that over-delivery is intentionally paid to the withdrawer so the 'all rounding favors the protocol' claim is not misleading.

findings.specText: story-043 commit a65dbf0: "minOut is derived from the same _creditedPrincipal(amount) expression so the swap floor and the credit cannot drift, keeping fairValue >= creditedPrincipal a provable solvency invariant." Mirrored in _creditedPrincipal NatSpec (lines 207-210): "...which is what makes `fairValueOfShares >= creditedPrincipal` a provable solvency invariant."
findings.specSource: git commit a65dbf0 body; ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol NatSpec lines 207-210
findings.actualBehavior: minOut = vault.convertToShares(creditedPrincipal); the swap guarantees sharesReceived >= minOut, so fairValue = convertToAssets(sharesReceived) >= convertToAssets(convertToShares(creditedPrincipal)). Because ERC4626 convertToShares and convertToAssets BOTH round down, convertToAssets(convertToShares(creditedPrincipal)) can be < creditedPrincipal by rounding dust, so the chain proves fairValue >= (a value possibly below creditedPrincipal), not fairValue >= creditedPrincipal.
findings.deviation: The story claims the solvency invariant is 'provable'; strictly it can be violated by sub-wei/few-wei ERC4626 double-round-down dust per deposit (accumulating on flat markets). The intent (conservative crediting) is faithfully implemented; only the absoluteness of the 'provable' claim is overstated.
findings.crossReference: Same rounding observation as code-scanner LOCAL-MKT-004 (local-low, solvency-invariant-rounding). Reported here only to make the story-claim overstatement visible in the spec-conformance report; not independently security-relevant.
findings.recommendation: Acknowledge the rounding dust in the invariant claim (fairValue >= creditedPrincipal - dust), or add a small protocol-favoring epsilon to minOut so the round-trip cannot dip below creditedPrincipal.

conformantStories.verdict: conformant (code) with a minor doc-staleness note
conformantStories.note: SurplusTracker/SurplusWithdrawer contracts/interfaces/tests are removed; no code in scope references them. However IYieldStrategy.sol NatSpec still names the deleted systems (line 49 'the SurplusTracker system', line 61 'the SurplusWithdrawer system'). Pure NatSpec staleness, QA-level, not a behavioural finding — surfaced for the qa-bundler, not as an F.

ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy buys shares on deposit (underlying->shares swap) and sells on withdraw (shares->underlying swap) via IAMMAdapter instead of vault.deposit()/redeem(); IAMMAdapter interface added. Matches the 'buy/sell vault tokens on the open market' intent for restriction-bearing vaults (sUSDe cooldown).

CurveAMMAdapter routes via Curve Router NG, stores one pre-computed route per ordered (tokenIn,tokenOut) pair, and swap() enforces the bidirectional invariant: reverts unless BOTH routes[in][out].configured AND routes[out][in].configured (lines 126-128). Does not reverse routes at runtime — matches the deliberate design. setRoute endpoint validation (path[0]==tokenIn, last-non-zero==tokenOut) is the only on-chain check; reverse-route INVERSE consistency is explicitly an off-chain/deploy-script trust assumption per the commit body and CLAUDE.md, so the .configured-flag-only check is faithful to stated intent (see code-scanner LOCAL-CRV-001/002 for the footgun lens).

Single skimSurplus(token,recipient) over the on-strategy EnumerableSet (base skimSurplus passes _authorizedClients.values()); ONE swap of aggregated totalShares; silent clamp replaced by the LOUD aggregate-surplus require (M-01 mitigation, line 464-467); empty client set is a no-op returning 0; backward-compatible authorizedClients(address) getter + getAuthorizedClients()/authorizedClientCount() present; principal untouched. Distinctness via EnumerableSet structurally closes M-01.

Per-client setAsideBufferSize (percent 0-100, default 0); owner-gated setSetAsideBuffer(client!=0, percent<=100) with SetAsideBufferSet event. Fast path (totalBufferShares==0) forwards full swap output to recipient unchanged. Buffered path redeems/swaps ONCE to self then sets aside underlyingReceived*bufferShares[i]/totalShares to each client and sends remainder (+dust) to recipient, returning the reduced amount; minOut still computed on full totalShares. Matches commit 5f9abdd intent.

Principal credited as amount*(MAX_BPS-slippageToleranceBps)/MAX_BPS for both clientBalances and totalDeposited; minOut derived from the same _creditedPrincipal value; Deposited event still emits the nominal amount. Conservative crediting is faithfully implemented; only the 'provable' qualifier on the solvency invariant is overstated (see FAITH-002).

_depositInternal returns creditedPrincipal; deposit() and depositAsOwner() both percolate it (previously void). IYieldStrategy.deposit and AYieldStrategy.deposit updated to returns(uint256 creditedPrincipal) with nominal-vs-credited NatSpec; market strategy returns the haircut, no accounting/withdraw/skim/Deposited-event changes. Matches commit 2306719 intent.

observationsNotFindings.detail: _emergencyWithdraw (lines 386-395) moves raw vault shares to owner without touching clientBalances/totalDeposited. No story specifies a principal update on emergency, so this is not a Law-2 faithfulness violation; it is the owner footgun already captured by code-scanner LOCAL-MKT-003 (totalBalanceOf overstates afterward; later withdrawers clamp on a shrunken share pool). Routed to the operational-hazard lane, not a faithfulness F.

Phase 1 caches state.balance = this.balanceOf(token,client) (principal), but ERC4626Market._totalWithdraw (lines 404-435) ignores the passed-in cached `amount` (using it only as the >0 guard) and zeroes/decrements by the LIVE clientBalances[client]. If principal changes during the 24h window the executed amount differs from the WithdrawalInitiated-announced balance. No story-036 acceptance criterion pins execution to the cached snapshot, and balance changes require protocol-owned client/owner action, so this is a documented quirk (profile note), not a faithfulness finding. Flagged for visibility only.
